correctness.rationale: The construction has a single cyclic clique and trees grafted only at clique vertices. In the non-rainbow case the consistent one-Lipschitz lift evolves by closed-neighborhood maxima, reaches consensus within graph diameter D, and an endpoint distance lift attains D. A rainbow clique rotates from time zero. In each graft, forced root height plus tree Lipschitzness bounds every vertex between b+t-depth and max(M,b+t-depth), with M<=b+H_tree, proving phase locking by H_tree+depth<=2H. Monotone-depth initial heights at a deepest leaf delay that leaf until t=2H, attaining sharpness. Inclusion-exclusion on clique colors gives exactly (3^c-3*2^c+3)/3 three-cycles; tree choices yield uniform 3^(k+1) basins, and global color symmetry yields 3^k(2^c-1) for each fixed point. Direct exhaustive checks passed for 269811 labelled states on 13 graphs; independently 7000 random seeded graphs passed lift/direct comparisons. No finite test is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Grafting arbitrary trees at clique vertices isolates an oscillator core from acyclic signal transport. The complete all-parameter theorem exhibits a topology-independent periodic-orbit census and individual basin law, in sharp contrast to a topology-sensitive stopping time governed by max(D,2H). The two independently attained clocks distinguish fast synchronization from delayed periodic phase locking, and arbitrarily deep grafts can nearly double the conservative diameter bound. The objects and invariants arise naturally from localized network perturbations, with unbounded tree branching and clique size; they are not a renamed elementary formula or an arbitrarily sliced finite census.
